_comment: Tool integration registry. Source of truth for which external tools the platform adopts. integration_audit.py validates this file. Hand-edited; no process writes it.

license_policy.import_rule: The repo carries no LICENSE file, so it is all-rights-reserved and client products may ship privately. GPL and AGPL code may not be imported by repo code. GPL or AGPL programs may run as separate command-line tools (subprocess), since that does not combine them with repo code.

tools.name: uv
tools.reason: Faster, cached installs in all 19 workflows; one pinned requirements lock per job family.

tools.name: ruff
tools.reason: Blocking only on syntax and undefined-name rules (E9,F63,F7,F82); style rules report-only.

tools.name: actionlint
tools.reason: Catches expression, trigger and shell errors across 19 workflows before push.

tools.name: zizmor
tools.reason: Workflow security audit: token scope (IOWA_DISPATCH_TOKEN, NASS_API_KEY), template injection, unpinned actions.

tools.name: pre-commit
tools.reason: Runs the constitution gates (LF, em-dash, leak audit blocking, node --check) on Price's machine before each commit.

tools.name: pytest
tools.reason: One parameterized runner over every module --selftest; reports selftest coverage (19 of 53 modules) as a number.

tools.name: Vale
tools.reason: Prose linter with Hawthorn rules: no em-dashes, scorekeeping blocklist, causal phrasing, undefined statistical terms.
tools.risk_notes: Complements leak_audit.py; leak_audit stays the blocking vocabulary gate.

tools.name: daff
tools.reason: Row and cell diff of master_opposition.csv per pipeline run, so outcome changes are reviewable.

tools.name: Dependabot
tools.reason: Version updates for pinned Actions and Python deps; replaces pip-audit and gitleaks (GitHub secret scanning already covers public repos).

tools.name: Pandera
tools.reason: Declarative schemas for master_opposition_clean.csv and county_policy_scores.csv: outcome enums, normalized State, 5-digit FIPS, lat/lon bounds, boolean coercion.
tools.risk_notes: Report-only until seven consecutive clean runs (configs/data_quality.json schema.mode = window), then blocking.

tools.name: normalize_state (in-house)
tools.reason: 51-entry map plus variants; chosen over the us package to avoid a dependency for a static table.

tools.name: column coverage delta gate (in-house)
tools.reason: Fails when a column's non-null count drops more than a set share versus the last snapshot; would have caught capacity_mw 123 to 3. Chosen over PyOD.

tools.name: out-of-fold label disagreement audit (in-house)
tools.reason: Flags county labels whose cross-fit probability strongly contradicts the label (confident-learning style). Chosen over cleanlab (AGPL).

tools.name: Internet Archive Save Page Now 2 and CDX APIs
tools.reason: Archives every Source URL; worklists and deliverables cite a durable snapshot when the original rots.
tools.risk_notes: Rate limited; nightly capped batch; free archive.org keys raise limits.

tools.name: trafilatura
tools.reason: Main text and publication date from candidate articles; date hints feed date_recovery worklists, never auto-applied.

tools.name: datasketch
tools.reason: MinHash LSH near-duplicate clustering so syndicated coverage of one hearing is one candidate event.

tools.name: civic-scraper
tools.reason: Maintained CivicPlus, Legistar, Granicus and PrimeGov adapters to raise jurisdiction resolution above the current handful of 808.

tools.name: OCRmyPDF
tools.reason: OCR layer for scanned agenda and minutes PDFs before the keyword pass over local_meeting_feed.py's agenda links. Chosen over Docling (model weight in CI). Spec 007 put the pass in agenda_text.py: no module read agenda PDFs before, so the pdfplumber pass this entry named did not exist.
tools.risk_notes: Needs apt tesseract-ocr and ghostscript in the job; agenda_text.py refuses to OCR without both and its selftest fails a workflow that runs it without installing them.

tools.name: pdfminer.six
tools.reason: Text-layer extraction that decides whether a PDF needs OCR, and the text for the keyword pass. Already a dependency of OCRmyPDF and the engine pdfplumber wraps, so it adds no install.

tools.name: Congress.gov API v3
tools.reason: Covers the 43 federal legislative records bill_sync skips; federal stays outside the state ladder.

tools.name: Epoch AI Frontier Data Centers
tools.reason: Project-level campuses with dates and power; baseline and announced-date cross-check.
tools.risk_notes: Frontier-only sample, biased to very large campuses; attribution required.

tools.name: LangExtract
tools.reason: Source-grounded extraction (character offsets) from agenda text into candidate rows; runs locally on Ollama, never in CI, output is a worklist.
tools.risk_notes: Model output is a draft; every field must carry its offset or it is dropped. Runs in CI by owner decision (commit 4a49585): agenda-extract.yml installs Ollama on the runner with gemma2:2b and passes --allow-ci; output is a draft worklist only. Spec 007 FR-005 originally said local only.

tools.name: firthmodels
tools.reason: Firth-penalized logistic as a candidate estimator for the rare blocked class (26 blocked, separation risk). firthlogist rejected: no Python 3.11 support, unmaintained since 2022.

tools.name: netcal
tools.reason: Session 5 (2026-10-01): its metrics module imports torch at load, and an install adds 57 packages including torch, pyro-ppl, gpytorch and tensorboard. The ECE, MCE, equal-mass variants and reliability bins it would supply are about 40 lines in calibration_gate.py with the same binary-label definitions (make versus take, docs/tool_selection.md rule 6; specs/008-model-robustness/research.md D3).

tools.name: esda + libpysal
tools.reason: Moran's I on county residuals and a state-grouped CV check that the AUC is not carried by same-state diffusion.
tools.risk_notes: Resolved in session 5: esda 2.9.0 declares Requires-Python >=3.11, so every workflow stays on 3.11 with no pin moved (specs/008-model-robustness/research.md D1). Pulls in geopandas, shapely and pyproj as dependencies.

tools.name: InterpretML (EBM)
tools.reason: Installed as interpret-core (the glassbox subset, without the dashboard stack); imports as interpret.glassbox. Glassbox challenger with exact per-variable shape functions for client-readable charts; promotes only through calibration_gate.py.

tools.name: skops
tools.reason: Model card per promoted model (data window, spec, metrics, gate result); safe persistence format.

tools.name: Census cartographic boundary counties 2024 (1:5m)
tools.reason: Current county geometry. The plotly geojson now used lacks 13 scored counties (9 Connecticut planning regions, 3 Alaska, Oglala Lakota SD).

tools.name: mapshaper
tools.reason: Build-time simplify and convert to TopoJSON; commits a small file into the repo instead of a 3.2 MB third-party fetch.

tools.name: topojson-client
tools.reason: Decodes the committed TopoJSON in the browser (stable, tiny).

tools.name: MapLibre GL JS
tools.reason: Vector basemap renderer under the existing Leaflet layers.

tools.name: maplibre-gl-leaflet
tools.reason: Binding that keeps every Leaflet page and plugin as is.

tools.name: OpenFreeMap
tools.reason: Free vector tiles, no key, no usage cap. Replaces Esri World Gray Canvas and OSM raster tiles, whose terms are a risk for client-facing commercial use.
tools.risk_notes: Keep current basemap as fallback in the chain.

tools.name: Tabulator
tools.reason: Sortable, filterable, CSV-exportable tables.

tools.name: Playwright
tools.reason: Smoke tests on every HTML/JS push: no error banner, markers present, county polygons at least 3,144. Closes the CI-inert UI gap.

tools.name: @axe-core/playwright
tools.reason: Accessibility check inside the same smoke tests; Lighthouse CI rejected as redundant.

tools.name: date range slider (in-house)
tools.reason: Filter pins by date with a range input. Chosen over Leaflet.TimeDimension (last release 2019).

tools.name: detail side panel (in-house)
tools.reason: County and project detail panel. Chosen over leaflet-sidebar-v2 (last release 2020).

tools.name: docxtpl
tools.reason: Fills the client-neutral location report template (templates/location_report.docx, Hawthorn styles, built from code) and optional per-client templates under templates/clients/<client>/ that bind the same fields; used unmodified as a library.
tools.risk_notes: LGPL-2.1, imported unmodified. Output passes validate.py --original against the template it was filled from; RichText cells use the {{r }} form.

tools.name: python-docx
tools.reason: Builds the Word templates from code (Hawthorn styles, no typed numbers) and reads rendered reports back for the checks; already installed as docxtpl's dependency, registered because repo code imports it directly.

tools.name: Jinja2
tools.reason: HTML template for county profile PDFs, autoescaped with StrictUndefined; already installed as docxtpl's dependency, registered because repo code imports it directly.

tools.name: MarkupSafe
tools.reason: Escapes link text and marks Great Tables and chart HTML safe inside the autoescaped Jinja2 PDF template; Jinja2's own escaping library.

tools.name: lxml
tools.reason: Reads rendered DOCX XML for the FR-002 checks (paraId limit, explicit tblGrid, hyperlinks beside runs) and the markdown twin; python-docx's own XML library.

tools.name: WeasyPrint
tools.reason: County profile PDFs from county-profile.html content.
tools.risk_notes: Needs the Pango system libraries (libpango-1.0-0, libpangoft2-1.0-0); the pipeline selftest job and render-county-pdf.yml install them, and the script prints the install line when they are missing.

tools.name: Great Tables
tools.reason: Publication-grade tables for PDFs and HTML briefs.
tools.risk_notes: PDF tables only; Word reports use native tables, which stay editable and accessible. Link cells are escaped before formatting (pandas 3 string columns reject its html() wrapper).

tools.name: Urban Institute Data Visualization Style Guide
tools.reason: Chart standard for policy audiences; reference only, viz-palette.js stays canonical.

tools.name: GitHub MCP server
tools.reason: Read Actions run logs and manifests directly instead of pulling tarballs to debug CI.

tools.name: U.S. Census Bureau Data API MCP
tools.reason: Superseded for now (2026-09-29): sessions reach api.census.gov directly through the environment network allowlist with CENSUS_API_KEY. The official MCP server is self-hosted and not in the connector directory.
tools.trigger: A session needs ACS queries the direct API cannot serve (complex table discovery, geography resolution), or the server becomes available as a hosted connector.

tools.name: ast-grep
tools.reason: Structural search and edit across ~100 modules; smaller diffs and fewer tokens than whole-file reads.

tools.name: DuckDB CLI
tools.reason: SQL re-derivation of deliverable statistics against the live CSV (Principle VI) without loading rows into context. Not a pipeline dependency.

tools.name: Bambi / PyMC
tools.trigger: A client question needs state-level partial pooling, or Python 3.12 is adopted pipeline-wide.
tools.reason: Hierarchical logistic; heavy install, slow in CI.

tools.name: crepes
tools.trigger: Class-conditional interval coverage is requested for the enacted class.
tools.reason: Mondrian conformal as a follow-up to the documented LAC zero-coverage finding.

tools.name: SetFit
tools.trigger: GDELT candidate volume exceeds what reviewers can triage weekly.
tools.reason: Few-shot relevance classifier; brings torch into CI.

tools.name: Media Cloud
tools.trigger: A GDELT recall audit is scheduled.
tools.reason: Second news index for recall cross-checks.

tools.name: faster-whisper + yt-dlp
tools.trigger: A named county posts meetings only as video and matters to a client.
tools.reason: Transcription is compute-heavy; pilot per county, run locally.

tools.name: OSM power features via Overpass
tools.trigger: The feature search needs a grid-proximity plugin.
tools.reason: Distance to 230 kV+ substations as a county or site variable; replaces discontinued HIFLD Open.

tools.name: WRI Aqueduct 4.0
tools.trigger: The drought source keeps failing in fetch-features.yml.
tools.reason: Water stress fallback; needs zonal stats from catchments to counties.

tools.name: edgartools
tools.trigger: Announced-date recovery needs company filings.
tools.reason: Company-level, not project-level; useful only for date hints.

tools.name: Turf.js
tools.trigger: Site reports need radius queries on the map.
tools.reason: Client-side within-distance queries.

tools.name: DuckDB-WASM
tools.trigger: Browser tables outgrow Tabulator's in-memory filtering.
tools.reason: In-browser SQL over Parquet.

tools.name: usaddress
tools.trigger: Geocode misses traced to unparsed Address strings.
tools.reason: Address parsing before the Census Geocoder ladder.

tools.name: Juriscraper
tools.trigger: dispute_watch.py needs state trial courts that CourtListener search lacks.
tools.reason: State court scrapers.

tools.name: ruptures
tools.trigger: The newsletter adds a surge or outlook section.
tools.reason: Changepoints in state event rates; descriptive only.

tools.name: Data Commons MCP
tools.trigger: Scouting new county plugin variables.
tools.reason: Agent-side statistics lookup.

tools.name: Polars
tools.reason: Data is 3.5 MB; pandas plus stdlib already fast enough.

tools.name: Ibis
tools.reason: No multi-backend need.

tools.name: SQLMesh
tools.reason: Same as dbt.

tools.name: Hamilton
tools.reason: Same as dbt; layers.json already declares lineage.

tools.name: Great Expectations
tools.reason: Pandera chosen; lighter and code-first.

tools.name: Soda Core
tools.reason: Pandera chosen.

tools.name: Scrapy / scrapy-playwright
tools.reason: civic-scraper plus existing adapters cover the portals.

tools.name: City Scrapers
tools.reason: civic-scraper covers the same platforms as a library.

tools.name: Crawl4AI
tools.reason: trafilatura covers article text.

tools.name: newspaper4k
tools.reason: trafilatura covers text and dates.

tools.name: feedparser / selectolax
tools.reason: local_meeting_feed.py already parses RSS and Granicus HTML.

tools.name: requests-cache / hishel
tools.reason: Modules use stdlib urllib with manifest skip logic.

tools.name: MarkItDown / unstructured / Camelot
tools.reason: pdfplumber plus OCRmyPDF chosen.

tools.name: Council Data Project
tools.reason: Full deployment stack (GCP); deferred whisper pilot covers the need.

tools.name: Bluesky firehose
tools.reason: Unverifiable and detection-biased. Local opposition groups organize mainly on Facebook, which has no free research access, so coverage would be thin and skewed.

tools.name: Common Crawl CC-NEWS
tools.reason: Terabyte-scale backfill for marginal gain.

tools.name: GovInfo / Regulations.gov
tools.reason: Federal Register API (deferred) covers the rulemaking need; these add bulk text without a product use.

tools.name: gridstatus as baseline
tools.reason: Generation queues are power plants, not data centers. Site-context use is deferred separately.

tools.name: LBNL Queued Up as baseline
tools.reason: Same category error; cost-layer use already scoped in the memo.

tools.name: HIFLD Open
tools.reason: Discontinued in 2025.

tools.name: NASS, EIA price, USGS water, Drought Monitor, PUDL generation
tools.reason: Shipped in fetch_county_features.py on 2026-09-28.

tools.name: cleanlab
tools.reason: AGPL-3.0; in-house out-of-fold disagreement audit does the same job at this scale.

tools.name: sentence-transformers / GLiNER / spaCy
tools.reason: MinHash covers dedupe and LangExtract covers extraction; BERTopic is deferred separately for the newsletter.

tools.name: Argilla / Label Studio / doccano / Baserow / Streamlit / Metabase / Rill / Superset
tools.reason: Hosting burden. Datasette covers read-only client databases and Grist (deferred) covers editable ones; the negative audit already has --next tooling (spec 003).

tools.name: Instructor / Outlines / BAML / DSPy / Snorkel / promptfoo / LiteLLM
tools.reason: LangExtract chosen as the single extraction layer.

tools.name: Langfuse / Opik / LLMLingua / vector stores
tools.reason: No production LLM stage in the pipeline.

tools.name: TOON
tools.reason: For flat tables CSV is already as compact; the gain applies to nested JSON the platform does not send.

tools.name: Repomix / code2prompt / gitingest / Serena
tools.reason: ast-grep plus targeted reads chosen; whole-repo packing costs more tokens than it saves.

tools.name: obra/superpowers
tools.reason: Spec Kit v1.0.12 already governs the development workflow.

tools.name: XGBoost / LightGBM / CatBoost / NGBoost / pyGAM
tools.reason: sklearn HistGradientBoosting already in feature_search; EBM chosen for glassbox shapes.

tools.name: statsmodels / PyFixest / glum / numpyro / ArviZ / Optuna / shapiq
tools.reason: Registered grid search with repeated CV already exists; firthmodels supplies intervals for the rare class.

tools.name: MLflow / DVC / whylogs / deepchecks / PiML / ydata-profiling
tools.reason: Snapshot manifest, calibration_history.csv and skops cards cover governance; deepchecks is AGPL.

tools.name: mgwr / spopt / tobler / h3
tools.reason: Overfits at county n with 327 positives; esda diagnostics only. osmnx is deferred separately for site reports.

tools.name: scikit-survival
tools.reason: GPL-3.0; lifelines already covers survival.

tools.name: addfips
tools.reason: GPL-3.0; gazetteer.py already maps county names to FIPS.

tools.name: us
tools.reason: In-house normalizer for a static 51-row table.

tools.name: PyOD
tools.reason: In-house coverage-delta and robust-z checks on three numeric columns.

tools.name: relplot
tools.reason: License string is a copyright line only. netcal was chosen over it, then itself eliminated in session 5 for its torch dependency; the metrics are built in-house.

tools.name: firthlogist
tools.reason: No Python 3.11 support; last release 2022; firthmodels chosen.

tools.name: statsforecast
tools.reason: Forecasting event volume invites forward claims the platform does not make.

tools.name: scoringrules
tools.reason: No probabilistic delay forecast exists (attributable delay is gated).

tools.name: Evidence / Datasette Lite / Mosaic / kepler.gl / deck.gl
tools.reason: Observable Framework (deferred) is the single static-app path and Datasette the database path; Datasette Lite would make client data public.

tools.name: Full MapLibre rewrite / protomaps-leaflet / Leaflet.VectorGrid
tools.reason: The MapLibre-Leaflet binding gives vector rendering without rewriting pages; PMTiles is deferred for large layers. VectorGrid is stale.

tools.name: Leaflet.TimeDimension / leaflet-sidebar-v2
tools.reason: Last releases 2019 and 2020; in-house equivalents chosen.

tools.name: Leaflet.heat
tools.reason: Density maps visually overstate detection-biased coverage.

tools.name: us-atlas
tools.reason: Pre-2022 county geometry repeats the Connecticut FIPS failure.

tools.name: ECharts / uPlot / Observable Plot / Altair / plotnine
tools.reason: Chart.js stays; no chart the pages need is missing.

tools.name: Alpine.js / Web Awesome / Lucide / MiniSearch / Fuse.js
tools.reason: Plain HTML with shared JS modules covers it; Pagefind is deferred for archive search.

tools.name: USWDS / GOV.UK Frontend / Primer / Carbon / Radix / IBM Plex
tools.reason: viz-palette.js plus Georgia is the house system; Urban guide kept as reference.

tools.name: Pym.js
tools.reason: Unmaintained, and iframe-resizer v5 is GPL. Client portal embeds use an in-house postMessage height script (about 30 lines) when needed.

tools.name: Lighthouse CI / pa11y-ci
tools.reason: axe-core inside Playwright chosen.

tools.name: ntfy
tools.reason: Apprise sends to ntfy and every other channel; Healthchecks is deferred.

tools.name: gitleaks / pip-audit / act
tools.reason: GitHub secret scanning and Dependabot are free and native.

tools.name: qsv / csvkit
tools.reason: DuckDB CLI and sqlite-utils cover it.

tools.name: Typst / Paged.js / Kaleido / marimo
tools.reason: docxtpl, Pandoc, WeasyPrint and Altair/vl-convert cover Word, PDF and chart export; Quarto is deferred.

tools.name: TimelineJS / StoryMapJS
tools.reason: Slow maintenance and Google Sheets coupling; vis-timeline (deferred) covers timelines.

tools.name: Zotero / Hypothes.is
tools.reason: Source URLs live in the CSV with archive snapshots.

tools.name: TabPFN
tools.reason: Deep learning is barred; newer versions restrict licensing.

tools.name: DoWhy / EconML / DiCE
tools.reason: Causal and counterfactual framing is barred client-side.

tools.name: Esri World Gray Canvas / OSM raster tiles (current)
tools.reason: Esri basemap terms and the OSM tile usage policy are risks for commercial client use; replaced by OpenFreeMap.

tools.name: MIT Election Data and Science Lab county presidential returns 2000-2024
tools.reason: Replaces county_votes.json, which the 2026-09-28 notices audit found was scraped from Townhall and Fox News and is not authoritative. A documented academic source makes the political variables defensible in client reports.
tools.risk_notes: Confirm Dataverse license terms at download; keep county_votes.json until parity is checked.

tools.name: Altair + vl-convert
tools.reason: One chart definition rendered as interactive Vega-Lite on web pages and as PNG or SVG in Word and PDF, with no browser in CI. Keeps the same chart consistent across static reports and client portals.

tools.name: Pandoc
tools.reason: Converts markdown briefs (county static reports, research memos) to branded Word through a reference template. Run as a separate program, so the GPL does not attach to repo code.
tools.risk_notes: CLI only; never linked or imported.

tools.name: Datasette
tools.reason: Read-only client databases with faceted browsing, full-text search, and CSV and JSON endpoints, built per client from the clean feed plus that client's watchlist config. This is the core of the active database product.
tools.risk_notes: Hosting and access control come from the deferred Cloudflare Access entry or a small container host; never expose group-level outcome columns.

tools.name: sqlite-utils
tools.reason: Builds each client SQLite from CSVs with typed columns, foreign keys and FTS in a few lines.

tools.name: Frictionless Data Package
tools.reason: Every client export ships a datapackage.json with schema, field definitions, sources and required attributions (Census, CC-BY, ODbL), then passes frictionless validate. It is a defensible, self-describing data product.

tools.name: Apprise
tools.reason: Library, no server: sends per-client watchlist alerts (new event, status change, hearing scheduled) to email, Slack or Teams from Actions.
tools.risk_notes: Alerts carry only verified or clearly labeled candidate items; vocabulary passes the leak audit.

tools.name: Observable Framework
tools.trigger: A client portal needs richer interactivity than the Leaflet pages give, built from Python data loaders.
tools.reason: Static data apps that can reuse pipeline modules as data loaders; one template, many client builds. Chosen over Evidence as the single static-app framework. Release pace slowed in 2026, so re-check maintenance at trigger time.

tools.name: Quarto
tools.trigger: One report must ship as Word, PDF and web from a single source.
tools.reason: Multi-format rendering with inline computed values (Principle VI).

tools.name: MJML
tools.trigger: Client alert digests are sent outside HubSpot.
tools.reason: Responsive email templates for per-client digests.

tools.name: Pagefind
tools.trigger: A client report archive or portal passes about 50 pages.
tools.reason: Static full-text search, no server.

tools.name: Grist (grist-core)
tools.trigger: A client needs to edit or annotate records (their own sites, internal notes) inside the database.
tools.reason: Spreadsheet-database with per-user access rules; self-host or hosted free tier.

tools.name: dbt-core + dbt-duckdb
tools.trigger: More than about five client databases need divergent views of the clean feed.
tools.reason: A downstream-only product layer of SQL views per client, tested and documented; never replaces the pipeline.

tools.name: Federal Register API
tools.trigger: A client asks for federal large-load or co-location rulemaking tracking.
tools.reason: No key needed; FERC and DOE rulemaking for a developer-facing policy product. Outside the opposition tracker itself.

tools.name: gridstatus (site context only)
tools.trigger: A site report needs grid context (wholesale prices, load forecasts, nearby generation queue).
tools.reason: Descriptive context for site reports; never a baseline or a model denominator.

tools.name: ERCOT large-load reports (context only)
tools.trigger: A Texas site report.
tools.reason: Zonal large-load queue context; aggregate only, never a baseline.

tools.name: National Zoning Atlas (site context only)
tools.trigger: A site report falls in a mapped jurisdiction.
tools.reason: Descriptive zoning context in reports; never a model feature (detection bias).

tools.name: BLS QCEW NAICS 518210 (context only)
tools.trigger: A report needs local data center employment context.
tools.reason: Suppression noted inline; never a model feature.

tools.name: osmnx
tools.trigger: Site reports add a proximity section (residences, schools, roads near the parcel).
tools.reason: Residential proximity is a core site risk question for developer clients.

tools.name: BERTopic
tools.trigger: The newsletter adds an emerging-concerns section.
tools.reason: Topic discovery beyond fixed is_* tags; runs locally, descriptive only.

tools.name: PMTiles + tippecanoe
tools.trigger: A map layer passes about 5 MB (parcels, transmission lines, client site layers).
tools.reason: Static vector tiles on any host; works with the MapLibre binding already selected.

tools.name: Perspective
tools.trigger: Client analysts want pivoting inside their portal.
tools.reason: WASM pivot grid over client data.

tools.name: Healthchecks
tools.trigger: An active database client is promised a freshness level.
tools.reason: Alerts when a scheduled refresh fails to run.

tools.name: changedetection.io
tools.trigger: The first active database client names jurisdictions whose pages have no API.
tools.reason: Watches specific county and PUC pages per client watchlist; self-host container.

tools.name: vis-timeline
tools.trigger: Project lifecycle timelines go into client case studies or portals.
tools.reason: Interactive lifecycle timelines for project-lifecycles.html and case studies.

tools.name: Cloudflare Pages + Access (free plan)
tools.trigger: The first private client portal or database.
tools.reason: Private hosting with email-based login for client portals; GitHub Pages cannot restrict access. Free plan user limit reported at 50; confirm at signup.

tools.name: dlt
tools.trigger: A client supplies a recurring feed (site lists, CRM exports) that must be loaded into their database.
tools.reason: Schema-evolving incremental loads into SQLite or DuckDB, downstream of the pipeline only.

tools.name: Docling
tools.trigger: Building the ordinance terms database (setbacks, noise limits, water and acreage caps as structured fields).
tools.reason: Best-in-class layout and table extraction from ordinance PDFs; run locally, not in CI.

tools.name: ArchiveBox (with SingleFile as CLI)
tools.trigger: A client deliverable needs firm-held evidentiary copies, or Wayback coverage or availability fails.
tools.reason: Local WARC and single-file copies of sources.

tools.name: LegiScan API
tools.trigger: A state bill tracking product launches, or Open States status disagreements pile up.
tools.reason: Independent status cross-check for client-facing bill tables (Principle III).

tools.name: FEMA National Risk Index
tools.trigger: A site report adds a physical risk section.
tools.reason: County hazard context developers expect; not a model feature.

tools.name: EPA ECHO air permits, EIA-860M planned generation, EIA-861/PUDL utility territory, Google News RSS proposal discovery
tools.reason: Shipped 2026-09-29 in fetch_air_permits.py, fetch_planned_generation.py, fetch_grid_territory.py and proposal_discovery.py (proposals-intel.yml; docs/passoff_2026-09-28_proposals_intelligence.md). Planned generation is spatial context near proposed projects only, never a baseline, consistent with the gridstatus elimination.

tools.name: Legistar matter probe and Google News status follow-up
tools.reason: Shipped 2026-09-28 in legistar_probe.py (configs/legistar_clients.json) and status_followup.py. Spec 007's civic-scraper work must reuse these for Legistar, not add a second Legistar path.

tools.name: GeoLibre
tools.reason: Authors whole-map project files (layers, styles, popups, legend, swipe) from Python, so pipeline outputs open as analyst-grade maps in the GeoLibre desktop app or Jupyter widget without hand styling.
tools.risk_notes: The public sharing host share.geolibre.app is forbidden (entry geolibre-share; integration_audit.py fails on any reference). Projects are opened locally only. Python 3.11+. The project schema is governed by this pin; the exporter re-validates every file with load_project and describe_project.

tools.name: forge3d (open core)
tools.reason: Path-traced terrain hero images from 3DEP elevation at print resolution, with Legend, ScaleBar, NorthArrow and text shaping in the open core; final composition stays in Pillow.
tools.risk_notes: Open core only; Pro features are forbidden: set_license_key, MapPlate, SVG/PDF vector export, building import, Mapbox style loading and scene bundles (entry forge3d-pro; integration_audit.py fails on any reference). Renders through wgpu; where it runs in CI is settled by plate-probe.yml (spec 013 US4).

tools.name: rasterio
tools.reason: Windowed HTTP range reads of USGS 3DEP cloud-optimized GeoTIFFs from the public staged-products bucket, so a county DEM is a few megabytes rather than whole 1-degree tiles. forge3d's own COG reader cannot open 3DEP (NAD83) without PROJ.
tools.risk_notes: Wheels bundle GDAL (MIT/X) and PROJ (MIT). Only used to fetch the DEM into the gitignored .cache/dem/; the render path itself never imports it.

tools.name: GeoLibre self-hosted web app
tools.trigger: An active_db client engagement needs an interactive analyst workspace behind access control.
tools.reason: The GeoLibre web app is a static build that could sit behind the spec 011 access-controlled host and load project files from private storage; see specs/012-geolibre-map-projects/research.md (R3). Until a client needs it, projects open locally only.

tools.name: share.geolibre.app
tools.reason: Public hosting of client data. Anything uploaded there is reachable by link, and client data may not be published on a public host (same rule as frontend-stacks). integration_audit.py fails on any reference in repo code.

tools.name: forge3d Pro (MapPlate, vector export, building import)
tools.reason: Commercial license key required (set_license_key). Composition is done in Pillow, PNG is the deliverable format, and buildings are out of scope. If a deliverable truly needs vector export that is a registry decision with a license purchase, not a code change. integration_audit.py fails on any reference in repo code.

product_lines.static_report: passive deliverables: location reports, county profile PDFs, briefs, newsletter content
product_lines.active_db: actively updated custom client databases: watchlists, alerts, filtered portals, exports
